source_summaries.title: Trump Was Right About the Corporate Media
source_summaries.summary: The White House Correspondents' Association dinner demonstrated how mainstream journalists normalize Donald Trump by choosing surrender over discomfort. Trump's core strategy relies on the assumption that opponents will always fold rather than face adversity. However, this approach ultimately contributed to a broader weakening of American global standing.

source_summaries.title: MAGA Mondays: Trump Goes on a Bizarre, Manic Posting Spree
source_summaries.summary: Will Sommer and Sam Stein hosted a live broadcast discussing Laura Loomer's trip to Ukraine and a conspiracy theory featured on Joe Rogan's show. They also covered Kash Patel allegedly using the FBI for self-promotion, Liz Truss partnering with Matt Schlapp, and Donald Trump's extensive social media posting over the weekend.

source_summaries.title: Triad Video Mailbag for July 31
source_summaries.summary: The Bulwark announced the return of its Triad Video Mailbag, hosted by JVL, releasing on July 31. Readers are invited to submit and upvote questions in the comments for the hosts to answer in the upcoming episode.

source_summaries.title: Trump Wanted to Kill. Then He Bombed.
source_summaries.summary: The United States abruptly paused its two-week bombing campaign against Iran to create space for peace talks, a decision reportedly prompted by concerns over dwindling munitions stockpiles. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump delivered a rambling, poorly received speech at the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner. The speech faced a cold reception from journalists, contrasting sharply with the constant adulation Trump typically receives from his supporters.

source_summaries.title: Why Did Trump Stop the Bombing?
source_summaries.summary: Following thirteen consecutive nights of U.S. bombing in Iran, President Trump abruptly halted the strikes, with reports suggesting dwindling missile interceptors as a primary factor. The pause highlights the strategic challenge of recognizing when military campaigns reach a culminating point of diminishing returns. Historical precedents, such as Operation Desert Storm, demonstrate the importance of halting military actions when political objectives have been met to avoid strategic overreach.

source_summaries.title: Special Delivery: Ukraine Blows Up ‘Russia’s Amazon’
source_summaries.summary: Ukraine launched nighttime drone strikes targeting at least nine warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, causing severe destruction and disrupting the country's e-commerce sector. Kyiv framed the attacks as retaliation for Russian strikes on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure and cited Wildberries' sale of military and dual-use goods. Analysts note the strikes are primarily intended to shatter the domestic Russian consensus that the war has no impact on daily life.

source_summaries.title: Historical accuracy is a surprisingly modern idea
source_summaries.summary: Christopher Nolan's adaptation of 'The Odyssey' has sparked right-wing complaints demanding greater historical accuracy in cinema. However, historical accuracy in filmmaking is a surprisingly modern concept, whereas past Hollywood epics routinely featured prominent white actors in non-white roles without similar outcry. Ultimately, cinematic entertainment and tradition have historically taken precedence over strict realism.

source_summaries.title: How Much Money Is Enough? Plus, Why AI Won’t Replace Financial Advisors — with Jack Raines
source_summaries.summary: Scott Galloway and Jack Raines discuss the definition of financial sufficiency and examine the economics of renting versus buying in expensive cities. They also explore the enduring value of financial advisors in the age of artificial intelligence, which can handle basic trade execution.

source_summaries.title: REPLAY: What is Going On inside Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon?
source_summaries.summary: U.S. strikes on Iran are currently paused as advisors express concern over depleted air defense munitions stockpiles in the Middle East, an issue U.N. Ambassador Mike Waltz has blamed on the Biden administration. Concurrently, the Pentagon has quietly lowered its official count of U.S. troops killed in the conflict, and reporting has revealed that Pete Hegseth's pick to lead the Navy was previously investigated by an inspector general.

source_summaries.title: After More Brutal Polls, Republicans Are Getting Uneasy About Trump
source_summaries.summary: Recent polling data ahead of the midterms shows Republicans trailing significantly on the generic ballot and facing low voter confidence on key economic and foreign policy issues. In response to these negative numbers, several Republican lawmakers have begun publicly distancing themselves from administration policies regarding Iran and military leadership. The declining poll numbers have sparked growing uneasiness within the GOP caucus regarding the toxicity of the party's current brand.

source_summaries.title: Big Tech Has $1.65 Trillion in Hidden AI Debt
source_summaries.summary: Recent U.S. tariffs and escalating conflict in Iran have driven Treasury yields to multi-year highs, raising concerns over inflation and the nation's growing debt burden. Meanwhile, an investigation reveals that major technology companies are carrying $1.65 trillion in hidden debt related to artificial intelligence.

source_summaries.title: How Big Tech Offloaded The Risk Of AI
source_summaries.summary: Scott Galloway and Ed Elson analyze the off-balance-sheet risks associated with Big Tech's massive artificial intelligence investments. They also discuss how rising oil prices and tariffs might sustain inflation, and suggest China is benefiting from conflict with Iran.

source_summaries.title: Six Networks.
source_summaries.summary: Beijing-based Moonshot AI is releasing the weights for its Kimi K3 model to allow developers to freely download, tweak, and host the technology. Founder Yang Zhilin aims to expand the company's user base and global influence through openness, contrasting with competing US proprietary systems. This move comes amid growing US concern regarding Chinese advancements in top-tier artificial intelligence development.

source_summaries.title: How Trump’s “America First” Administration Could Shut U.S. Scientists Out of the Next Nobel-Worthy Discovery
source_summaries.summary: A proposed rule by the Trump administration's Office of Management and Budget would grant political appointees sweeping authority to direct and terminate federal grants, including funding for major scientific research. Critics and researchers warn that restricting international collaboration and injecting political oversight into grant distribution will cause the United States to lose its leadership in global scientific discoveries.

source_summaries.title: Why the Supreme Court decided the wrong issue in the transgender athletes cases
source_summaries.summary: In West Virginia v. B.P.J., the Supreme Court upheld state bans on transgender girls participating in female sports under Title IX and the 14th Amendment. The author argues the court reached the wrong conclusion due to fundamental confusion over whether the plaintiffs were challenging sex segregation itself or the legal definition of biological sex.

source_summaries.title: Justices’ lucrative book deals deserve more scrutiny
source_summaries.summary: Supreme Court justices have collectively earned over $13 million from lucrative book deals, far exceeding their outside income limits and other gifts. These substantial earnings, heavily driven by their judicial positions and increasingly published by partisan outfits, warrant greater scrutiny from court-watchers.

source_summaries.title: How predictable is the Supreme Court from oral argument?
source_summaries.summary: An analysis of 56 Supreme Court cases from the 2025-2026 term examines how accurately oral arguments predict voting outcomes. The study finds that heavier questioning from justices provides meaningful signals of skepticism, correctly predicting a majority of individual votes and case outcomes. However, oral argument alone remains an imperfect predictor, as some cases defy initial impressions or yield unexpected coalitions.

source_summaries.title: Announcing The SCOTUSblog Summit: 2026 Term Preview
source_summaries.summary: SCOTUSblog and Johns Hopkins University are hosting a preview summit for the Supreme Court's 2026 term on September 16 at the JHU Bloomberg Center in Washington, D.C. The in-person event features a live podcast recording, a keynote address, and a panel discussion with prominent corporate general counsels.
